title: How a CPU runs an instruction
examples: What happens inside a CPU when it runs a program?

explain.say: A CPU does one tiny job at a time, incredibly fast. It fetches an instruction from memory, decodes it, executes it and moves on, repeating this loop billions of times every second.

faq.a: It is the loop every CPU repeats: fetch the next instruction from memory, decode what it means, execute it, then move the program counter on to the next one. Every program, from games to web pages, runs as billions of these tiny steps.
asks: How does a CPU run a program?
What does fetch mean in a CPU?

faq.q: What does the control unit do?
faq.a: The control unit is the CPU's organiser. It decodes each instruction and sends signals telling the other parts, like the ALU and the registers, what to do and when.
asks: What does decode mean in a CPU?

faq.a: The ALU, or arithmetic logic unit, is the part of the CPU that does maths and logic: adding, subtracting, comparing and true-or-false tests. Everything a computer does is built from these simple operations.
asks: What does the arithmetic logic unit do?
What does execute mean in a CPU?

faq.a: A register is a tiny store inside the CPU that holds a number being worked on right now. Registers are much faster than RAM, but there are only a few dozen of them. One special register, the program counter, holds the address of the next instruction.

faq.q: What does the clock speed of a CPU mean?
faq.a: The clock is a signal that ticks to keep every step in time. A 3 gigahertz CPU ticks 3 billion times a second. Most chips also have several cores, each running its own fetch-decode-execute loop at once.

facts: A 3 GHz processor's clock ticks 3 billion times per second.
The stored-program idea behind the fetch-decode-execute cycle was described by John von Neumann in 1945.

quiz.say: Which part of the CPU actually adds two numbers together?
quiz.why: The arithmetic logic unit does the maths and logic; the other parts organise and keep track.

wrong.0: The control unit decodes instructions and directs the other parts, but does not do the sums.
wrong.2: The program counter only holds the address of the next instruction.

quiz.say: What happens straight after an instruction is fetched?
quiz.why: The control unit decodes the instruction to work out what it means before it can be executed.

wrong.1: The cycle simply carries on; nothing restarts.
wrong.2: Instructions are worked on inside the chip, not printed.
